items.followUp: If two algorithms both give the correct answer, what factors can you compare to decide which is more efficient?

rubric.why: The choice must be made among algorithms that solve the problem correctly.
rubric.description: Compare only algorithms that produce a correct solution.
rubric.how: States that each algorithm must solve the problem correctly.

rubric.why: An efficient algorithm should use less time to complete the task.
rubric.description: Compare the time taken by the algorithms.
rubric.how: Mentions execution time or speed as a comparison factor.

rubric.why: Algorithms can differ in the amount of memory or storage they require.
rubric.description: Compare memory or space requirements.
rubric.how: Mentions memory, space, or storage use as a comparison factor.

rubric.why: The comparison should lead to selecting the algorithm that meets the requirements while using resources efficiently.
rubric.description: Choose the algorithm that solves the problem correctly with the least required resources.
rubric.how: States that the most efficient suitable algorithm should be selected.

modelAnswer: Check that each algorithm solves the problem correctly.
Compare how much time each algorithm takes.
Compare the memory or space each algorithm requires.
Choose the suitable algorithm that uses resources most efficiently.

items.followUp: Name two ways to protect information sent during online banking.

rubric.why: Encryption is the central method used to protect data transmitted over the internet.
rubric.description: Explain that encryption protects online information.
rubric.how: States that encryption converts information into a coded form.

rubric.why: Coded data is harder for unauthorized people to read or use.
rubric.description: Describe protection from unauthorized access or reading.
rubric.how: Mentions that encrypted information cannot easily be understood by unauthorized users.

rubric.why: Internet users share personal and sensitive information online.
rubric.description: Connect encryption to privacy and sensitive information.
rubric.how: Gives privacy or protection of personal/confidential information as a benefit.

rubric.why: Encryption supports safer everyday activities that involve sending information online.
rubric.description: Give an everyday internet use made safer by encryption.
rubric.how: Names online banking, shopping, or another secure internet activity.

modelAnswer: Encryption changes information into a coded form while it is sent over the internet.
This helps prevent unauthorized people from reading or accessing the information.
It protects the privacy of personal and sensitive details.
It helps make everyday activities such as online banking and shopping more secure.

items.followUp: How can acting out a situation help you understand a problem before writing its solution?

rubric.why: Act it out means representing the problem through actions or a simulation.
rubric.description: Explain the method of acting out the problem.
rubric.how: States that the solver acts out, role-plays, or simulates the situation.

rubric.why: Acting out can clarify what happens and help determine a solution.
rubric.description: Explain how acting out helps plan a solution.
rubric.how: Connects the activity to understanding the steps or finding a solution.

modelAnswer: Act it out means acting or simulating the situation described in the problem.
It helps us understand the sequence of events and plan a suitable solution.

items.followUp: Write two other steps that may be used when solving a problem.

rubric.why: Identifying or defining the problem is a valid problem-solving step.
rubric.description: State one valid step: identify or define the problem.
rubric.how: Names problem identification or definition.

rubric.why: Any one of these is another valid step in the problem-solving process.
rubric.description: State a second valid problem-solving step.
rubric.how: Names a suitable step such as analysis, design, implementation, testing, or evaluation.

modelAnswer: Identify and define the problem.
Design, implement, test, or evaluate a solution.

items.followUp: What should you consider when comparing two possible solutions to a problem?

rubric.why: Selecting a solution requires comparing alternatives against the problem's requirements or criteria.
rubric.description: Compare possible solutions against requirements or criteria.
rubric.how: Mentions comparing solutions using requirements or criteria.

rubric.why: The selected option should be practical and meet the requirements effectively.
rubric.description: Choose the most suitable solution.
rubric.how: States that the best, effective, efficient, or feasible option should be selected, optionally considering resources.

modelAnswer: Compare the possible solutions against the problem's requirements and criteria.
Select the solution that is most effective and feasible with the available resources.

items.followUp: Which HTML attribute is commonly used with the font tag to set text colour?

rubric.why: The font tag is the HTML tag used to specify font presentation in basic HTML.
rubric.description: Identify the font tag.
rubric.how: Names the font tag.

rubric.why: The tag can specify properties such as size, colour, or typeface.
rubric.description: State a property controlled by the font tag.
rubric.how: Names at least one of size, colour, or typeface (face).

modelAnswer: The <font> tag is used to change the appearance of text.
Its attributes can set the text size, colour, and typeface.

items.followUp: What does the href attribute specify in an anchor tag?

rubric.why: The opening and closing a tags form an anchor element.
rubric.description: Identify the element as the anchor tag.
rubric.how: Names the a tag or anchor tag.

rubric.why: The anchor element creates a link to another location or resource.
rubric.description: Explain the purpose of the anchor tag.
rubric.how: States that it creates a hyperlink or link to a destination.

modelAnswer: The ... tag is called the anchor tag.
It is used to create a hyperlink to another page, file, or location.

items.followUp: Give one example of information usually kept in storage rather than temporary memory.

rubric.why: Memory temporarily holds data and instructions currently needed by the computer.
rubric.description: Describe the role of memory.
rubric.how: Mentions temporary or current-use data, or that memory is volatile.

rubric.why: Storage keeps data for longer periods and retains it when power is off.
rubric.description: Describe the role of storage.
rubric.how: Mentions long-term or non-volatile saving of files or data.

modelAnswer: Memory temporarily holds the data and instructions currently being used by the computer.
Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use, even when the power is off.
